newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat seedbed preparation behind average.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat seedbed preparation behind average.

text.p: Seedbed preparations in Oklahoma wheat fields were behind average during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.
The report said recent rain had slowed seedbed preparations and seedings for the 1997 wheat crop.
Seedbed preparations advanced to 42 percent, compared to 54 last year and 56 for the five-year average.
All row crops with the exception of corn were progressing ahead of the five-year average. Corn was 21 percent mature, ahead of 18 last year but behind the average of 43 percent.

Twenty-one percent of the sorghum crop was listed as mature, compared to five percent for both last year and the average. Sorghum condition was rated 91 percent good to excellent, seven percent fair and two percent poor.

Bolls were opening on eight percent of the cotton acreage, versus nil last year and four percent on average. Cotton condition was rated 61 percent good to excellent, 26 percent fair and 13 percent poor to very poor.
Pasture and range condition was rated 68 percent good to excellent, 26 fair and six percent poor.
